prompt.context: Our client is an Amsterdam-based retail bank that has seen exceptional growth in the last 5 years. They are involved in commercial banking, investment banking, and wealth management. Currently, they are looking to acquire another bank in Europe. The CEO has hired our firm to help identify an ideal acquisition target.
prompt.question: Help the CEO identify the ideal acquisition target from the candidates available.

clarifying_info.q: Is there a specific metric to measure success?
clarifying_info.a: There is no specific metric defined for success.

clarifying_info.q: What is the rationale for the acquisition?
clarifying_info.a: The rationale is to expand outside Amsterdam.

clarifying_info.q: Are they open to targets with different financial products?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, they are open to acquiring organizations with the same or different financial products.

clarifying_info.q: What is the size of Bank Co?
clarifying_info.a: Bank Co has 600K customers and $10B in assets under management.

exhibits.title: Acquisition Targets Overview
exhibits.shows: A table comparing three acquisition targets (Bank A, Bank B, Bank C), all located in Luxembourg, across three metrics.

data.note: All targets are located in Luxembourg

framework: 1. Market Attractiveness: market size, market growth, consumer trends
2. Financial Attractiveness: revenue, costs (fixed and variable)
3. Synergies: product synergies, consumer synergies, cost synergies
4. Risks: brand erosion, culture integration, regulatory environment

questions.prompt: Looking at Exhibit 1, what are your initial insights about the three acquisition targets?
questions.guidance: Candidate should note: (1) Targets vary in size from smaller than Bank Co (Bank C: 300K) to larger (Bank B: 800K); (2) There is a visible trend that smaller firms have higher average products sold per customer (Bank C: 6.1, Bank A: 4.3, Bank B: 3.4); (3) Average profitability per customer does not follow a clear size trend, suggesting differences in business model/operations.

questions.prompt: What are the advantages and disadvantages of acquiring these firms based on size?
questions.guidance: Smaller firm (Bank C): easier to manage post-acquisition, less financial capital required, but slower market entry. Larger firm (Bank B): enables faster market entry and scale, but harder to manage and requires more capital. Market perception varies. Any logical reasoning is acceptable.

questions.prompt: Why do you think the average products sold per customer differ across the three targets?
questions.guidance: Smaller firms may offer better customization and customer service, leading to higher cross-sell. Larger firms may have a higher number of products covering broad customer segments but lower penetration per customer. Better salesforce/products at smaller scale. Any logical reason is acceptable.

questions.prompt: Why does the average profitability per customer differ across the three targets?
questions.guidance: Higher price per product, better cost management (ask candidate to split into fixed/variable), better talent productivity, better financial management, better overhead management. Any logical reason is acceptable.

questions.prompt: Based on the data in Exhibit 1, which bank are you most inclined to acquire and why?
questions.guidance: Any answer is acceptable with sound logic. Candidate should weigh size, profitability per customer, and products per customer. Prompts structured thinking about trade-offs before the quantitative question.

questions.prompt: Bank Co has 600K customers and average profitability of $160 per customer. What would be our combined profitability per customer if we acquire Bank A vs. Bank B vs. Bank C? Assume no synergies.
questions.guidance: Candidate should compute total profit for each entity, sum profits, sum customers, then divide. Bank A and Bank C yield the same combined profitability (~$130/customer) and are superior to Bank B (~$120/customer).

math.setup: Combined profitability/customer = (Bank Co total profit + Target total profit) / (Bank Co customers + Target customers)
math.answer: Bank A and Bank C both yield approximately $130/customer combined profitability; Bank B yields ~$120/customer. Bank A and Bank C are preferred on this metric.

questions.prompt: Bank A and Bank C yield the same profitability per customer. What other factors would you consider to decide between them?
questions.guidance: Candidate should explore Synergies and Risks. Financial synergies (revenue): ease of capturing customers, cross-sell/up-sell opportunities from different products, price increase if monopoly. Financial synergies (cost): consolidation of branches, labor, and overheads. Non-financial synergies: specialization sharing (customer service, product innovation), process optimization at scale, brand presence as a multinational bank leading to higher stock price. Risks: regulatory requirements in Luxembourg vs. Amsterdam must be verified; culture integration challenge; brand perception if target has a poor reputation. Any logical reason is acceptable.

brainstorming.prompt: What synergies and risks should Bank Co consider when choosing between Bank A and Bank C?

categories.name: Financial Synergies - Revenue
ideas: Ease of capturing new customers in Luxembourg
Cross-sell/up-sell opportunities if product sets differ
Potential price increase in case of reduced competition

categories.name: Financial Synergies - Cost
ideas: Reduction in overhead and administrative costs

categories.name: Non-Financial Synergies
ideas: Brand presence as a multinational bank increasing stock price

categories.name: Risks
ideas: Regulatory: verify Luxembourg banking regulations and impact on operations
Culture: integration of two distinct organizational cultures
Brand: assess target bank's current reputation and public perception

recommendation: Acquire either Bank A or Bank C — both yield equivalent combined profitability per customer of approximately $130.
If synergies are the deciding factor, prefer the target that offers the greatest complementary product set or cost consolidation opportunity.
risks: Regulatory compliance in Luxembourg may impose new constraints on Bank Co's operations.
Cultural integration could slow post-merger performance and erode employee retention.
Poor brand reputation of the target could negatively affect Bank Co's image.
next_steps: Conduct detailed due diligence on Luxembourg banking regulations.
Assess product overlap/gap between Bank Co and each target to quantify cross-sell synergies.
Evaluate cultural fit through management interviews and organizational assessment.
Model explicit synergy scenarios with and without cost consolidation to sharpen the final recommendation.
